prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a passenger and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1180; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas, where Driver 1 was stopped in traffic when the front of Driver 2's vehicle struck the rear bumper of Driver 1's car. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy for that vehicle. A passenger, identified in this report only as Passenger, was seated in the front right position and reported pain in the left knee after the impact. Responding officers confirmed Passenger was present in the vehicle at the time of the crash, and both drivers and two independent witnesses gave consistent accounts of how the collision happened. Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the rear of Driver 1's vehicle and the front of Driver 2's vehicle, and the extent of that damage fits the reported force of the impact. Driver 1 stated the car had no prior damage that he was aware of, and nothing observed at the scene suggested otherwise. The knee injury described by Passenger is consistent with the way a passenger's leg would strike the dashboard or lower console in a collision of this kind. Passenger was transported for evaluation, and the report will be updated if additional information becomes available.
